results.message: Why did your bishops meet in councils?

voice_event.speaker: lpc
voice_event.text:
Bishops met in councils to judge what had to be decided together, where one man could not rule alone. Some questions reached beyond one bishop's own seat, and they had to be argued in the open, among colleagues. One was how to receive those who had failed under persecution. Another was whether a baptism given outside our one church counted at all. A third was what a bishop could do when a presbyter openly defied him. Councils met to settle these, and they left their rulings in writing.

The weight those councils carried, we answered twice, in ways that do not agree. At the council of 256, Cyprian opened with this: “None of us sets himself up as a bishop over other bishops, and none of us uses a tyrant's terror to force a colleague into obedience. Every bishop has his own right to judge, in keeping with the freedom and power allowed to him. He can no more be judged by another bishop than he himself can judge another. Instead, let us all wait for the judgment of our Lord Jesus Christ. He is the only one who has the power both to place us in the government of His Church and to judge how we conduct ourselves there.”

One held that each bishop judges for himself and answers to Christ alone. The other held that smaller councils yield to wider ones, and even the widest can later be corrected. We keep both as ours, because both are.

names.name: Thascius Caecilius Cyprianus, bishop of Carthage (248/249-258)

figures_used.bridge_line: Our bishop, chosen while still new to the faith, over his own reluctance. During a plague he taught us to love even our enemies. He was put to death under Valerian.

dates.display: a trained rhetorician who turned from a public career to Christian life, converted c. 246; ordained and elected bishop of Carthage between roughly July 248 and April 249 by the acclamation of the Carthaginian people, over the recorded opposition of five presbyters, while still newly baptised, as his deacon Pontius tells it; banished to Curubis under the Valerianic persecution; executed under the emperor Valerian in 258
